title: Embeddings API
pitch: OpenAI-compatible text embeddings: E5-small-v2 (384 dims) on Mojo CPU kernels, $0.02 per million tokens
example:
curl https://embed.mojojojo.cc/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOJOJOJO_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":["how do I reset my password"],"input_type":"query"}'
notes: input_type is "query" or "passage" (E5 prefixes are added for you); default passage.
Vectors are L2-normalised, 384 dimensions; up to 512 inputs of 20,000 characters per request.
Matches the PyTorch reference to 2e-7 max abs difference (cosine 0.9999999).
Speed: 0.40x PyTorch at batch 1 up to 0.93x at batch 200 on 2 pinned cores. It is a convenience and price play, not a latency win.

tools.name: embed_text
tools.description: Embed one or more texts with E5-small-v2 (384-dim, L2-normalised). Use input_type=query for search queries and passage for documents.

input: how do I reset my password

title: Image Moderation API
pitch: NSFW image classification on a Mojo ViT, $1 per thousand images, no image retention
notes: Send the raw image, a multipart field named file, or JSON {"images_base64":[...]}. Up to 8 images, 50 megapixels each.
Returns normal/nsfw probabilities and flagged (nsfw >= 0.5). A binary classifier: it does not detect violence, minors or text.
Logits match PyTorch to 5.5e-06.
Speed: 0.65x PyTorch (about 2 images/s on 2 cores). Images are decoded in memory and never written to disk.

tools.name: moderate_image
tools.description: Classify images as normal or nsfw. Images are base64-encoded png/jpeg/webp/gif/bmp.

title: Rerank API
pitch: Cohere-style reranking with the MiniLM-L6 cross-encoder on Mojo CPU kernels, $10 per million pairs
example:
curl https://rerank.mojojojo.cc/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOJOJOJO_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"capital of france","documents":["Paris is the capital.","Bananas are yellow."],"top_n":1}'
notes: Scores are raw cross-encoder logits (higher is more relevant); not comparable across queries.
Up to 512 documents per request; each document is truncated to 512 tokens with the query.
Max logit difference to PyTorch 2.9e-06.
Speed: 0.34x PyTorch at batch 1, 0.89x at batch 200. English MS MARCO passages only; evaluate on your own data.

tools.name: rerank_documents
tools.description: Score documents against a query with a MiniLM cross-encoder and return them best first (higher logit is more relevant).

documents: Paris is the capital of France.
Lyon is a city in France.

title: Tabular Score API
pitch: Train a tree ensemble on your rows, then score at up to 570x scikit-learn's single-row speed on Mojo kernels
model: scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting + ExtraTrees, exported to the Mojo forest kernel
example:
curl https://score.mojojojo.cc/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOJOJOJO_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"churn","target":"churned","rows":[{"age":31,"plan":"pro","churned":"no"}, ...]}'

curl https://score.mojojojo.cc/v1/models/churn/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOJOJOJO_KEY" \
  -d '{"rows":[{"age":44,"plan":"free"}]}'
notes: Binary targets only; up to 200,000 rows and 200 feature columns; training is capped at 120 seconds. Rows with numbers and strings; missing values are imputed.
Models are private to your account. The response includes a holdout AUC from a 80/20 split when you send at least 100 rows.
Serving is exact: probabilities match scikit-learn to 1e-15 on the shipped benchmark models.
Speed versus scikit-learn on 2 cores: 12-570x at batch 1, 2-8x at batch 64-1024, 1.0-4x at batch 8192 (gradient boosting is only 1.03x at large batch).
Not for credit, hiring, insurance or medical decisions.

tools.name: train_model
tools.description: Train a binary classifier on rows (list of objects) and the target column name; returns holdout AUC. Models are private to your account.

tools.name: predict
tools.description: Score rows with a trained model; returns probability of the positive class and a label per row.

title: Speech-to-Text API
pitch: Whisper tiny.en transcription on Mojo CPU kernels, OpenAI-compatible, $0.003 per audio minute
notes: wav, flac or ogg; mono-mixed and resampled to 16 kHz; up to 300 seconds per request, decoded in 30 second windows.

English only, smallest Whisper model: expect visibly more errors than larger models. No word error rate is claimed; parity was checked only as identical greedy tokens versus Hugging Face on synthetic clips.
Speed: 0.93x PyTorch end to end (32 tokens), 0.71x on the encoder.
Audio is decoded in memory and never written to disk.

tools.name: transcribe_audio
tools.description: Transcribe English speech (wav/flac/ogg, base64, up to 300 s) with Whisper tiny.en.
